window_text.11: God did extraordinary miracles through Paul,
window_text.12: so that even handkerchiefs and aprons that had touched him were taken to the sick, and their illnesses were cured and the evil spirits left them.

blind.question: What leaves the sick?

assessments.reason: Verse 12 states “the evil spirits left them,” where “them” refers to the sick; thus the answer matches the key.

blind.reason: The text explicitly says “the evil spirits left them,” referring to the sick.

reader.contrast: Evil spirits left the sick, whereas their illnesses were cured.
reader.reason: The reader must distinguish the subject of “left” from the separate condition that was cured.

editor.contrast: Evil spirits left the sick, whereas their illnesses were cured.
editor.reason: The parallel outcomes could be confused, but the passage explicitly assigns leaving to the evil spirits and curing to the illnesses.

items.question: Why do the seven sons run out of the house?
items.answer: because the man with the evil spirit beat them
items.competitor: because they told the spirit to leave

window_text.13: Some Jews who went around driving out evil spirits tried to invoke the name of the Lord Jesus over those who were demon-possessed. They would say, “In the name of the Jesus whom Paul preaches, I command you to come out.”
window_text.14: Seven sons of Sceva, a Jewish chief priest, were doing this.
window_text.15: One day the evil spirit answered them, “Jesus I know, and Paul I know about, but who are you?”
window_text.16: Then the man who had the evil spirit jumped on them and overpowered them all. He gave them such a beating that they ran out of the house naked and bleeding.

items.original_question: Why do the seven sons run out of the house?
items.original_answer: because the man with the evil spirit beat them

blind.question: Why do the seven sons run out of the house?

readings.answer: Because the man with the evil spirit beat them so badly.
readings.support: He gave them such a beating that they ran out of the house

assessments.reason: Verse 16 says, “He gave them such a beating that they ran out of the house,” matching the answer that they ran because the man with the evil spirit beat them.

blind.reason: The passage explicitly states they ran out because the demon-possessed man beat them.

reader.quote: He gave them such a beating that they ran out of the house naked and bleeding.
reader.contrast: The immediate cause of their flight was the beating, not their earlier command for the spirit to leave.
reader.reason: The passage explicitly links the man's attack and beating to the sons running from the house.

editor.quote: He gave them such a beating that they ran out of the house naked and bleeding.
editor.contrast: The sons’ command to the spirit initiated the confrontation, but the man’s beating them is the direct reason they fled.
editor.reason: The question clearly asks for the cause of their running away. The quoted cause-and-result construction uniquely supports the key.
